requirements.requirement: opsadmin configured on node1 with SSH access using the specified ed25519 public key
requirements.summary: opsadmin user was created, and /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys contains exactly the specified public key with correct 700/600 permissions and ownership. Verified both before and after the mandatory restart (boot_id changed from 71f12f87... to e34f7470...), confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disallow password authentication)
requirements.summary: sshd_config was set with PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes; sshd -T confirms the effective config both pre- and post-restart. opsadmin's password was locked (shadow entry '!'), and a live SSH attempt to opsadmin@node1 was rejected with only publickey/gssapi offered, both before and after the reboot, demonstrating the control is enforced and persistent.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (baseline, restart, boot-identity change, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, uptime, sshd active state, and authorized_keys content. systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged with stream closure. Polling through connection timeouts/resets confirmed the node went down and came back. Post-restart boot_id (e34f7470...) differs from baseline (71f12f87...) and uptime reflects the new boot time. sshd, opsadmin's key, locked password, and pubkey-only sshd config were all re-verified as intact post-restart, matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity/listening-sockets snapshot cross-check.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — configuring opsadmin with the specified ed25519 key and enforcing key-based-only SSH authentication — are directly and coherently satisfied by pre- and post-restart evidence, including a live SSH attempt confirming only publickey/gssapi methods are offered. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly with a verified boot-identity change and full recovery of the configured state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only blemish is a small leftover placeholder file in /tmp from a verification step that was not cleaned up.
limitations: No test of an actual private-key SSH login succeeding was performed (executor lacked the corresponding private key), so acceptance of valid pubkey auth is inferred from sshd -T config and denial-of-non-key-auth evidence rather than a successful key login.
The /tmp/keytest/id_ed25519 placeholder residue is low-risk but was left in place rather than cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were largely purposeful: user/key setup, sshd hardening with a pre-edit backup of sshd_config (a reasonable, low-risk safety practice), password lock, config validation, and a bounded restart-evidence protocol. One minor unnecessary mutation: cmd-42fea6a1be184ccc created /tmp/keytest/id_ed25519 (a placeholder file, not an actual usable private key) during a verification step, and it was never cleaned up — it is still present in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. This is low-risk residue (a placeholder text file) but was not restored. The sshd_config.bak.<timestamp> backup is also residue in /etc/ssh but represents a defensible operational safety practice before modifying a security-critical config, so it is not penalized as unnecessary. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and package health remained consistent (dnf) before and after.
